slides.title: Subho Bijoya: what to say, and to whom
slides.sub: Pranam, kolakuli, mishti and the messages

slides.title: Auspicious victory
slides.body: Subho Bijoya means auspicious victory: Durga's victory over Mahishasura. Say it only after the immersion. Before that, it's Sharodiya shubhechha or Happy Durga Puja.

slides.title: More than a phrase
items: Bijoyar chithi: letters to elders far away

slides.title: Wishes to send
items: Accept my Bijoya pranam and my love.
শুভ বিজয়ার প্রণাম ও ভালোবাসা নিও।
Ma will come again; until then, stay well.
মা আবার আসবেন, ততদিন ভালো থেকো, হাসিখুশি থেকো।
The dhak is quiet; may the joy last all year.
ঢাকের আওয়াজ থেমে গেল, কিন্তু মনের আনন্দ থাকুক সারা বছর।
Pranam to the elders, love to the little ones.
বড়দের প্রণাম, ছোটদের ভালোবাসা। শুভ বিজয়া!

slides.title: When someone says it to you
slides.body: Just say Subho Bijoya back. To an elder, add pranam. To someone younger, add ashirbad (blessings) or bhalobasha (love).

slides.title: For colleagues and clients
slides.body: Warm Bijoya greetings to you and your family. May the year ahead bring good health and success.

slides.title: A call beats a forward
slides.body: A call or a visit with a box of sweets still means more than a forwarded image. People visit the relatives and neighbours they owe a Bijoya call, and some families keep it up for weeks.

slides.title: Who's getting your first pranam?

caption.en:
Subho Bijoya wishes after Durga Puja 2026: what Kolkata says, and when 🙏

Subho Bijoya means auspicious victory. You say it only after the immersion, from Dashami evening, which was Wednesday 21 October this year. Before that it's Sharodiya shubhechha.

Then comes the custom: pranam to elders, kolakuli with friends, sweets for every visitor, and calls to the relatives you owe a Bijoya visit. To an elder, add pranam. To someone younger, ashirbad or bhalobasha.

We wrote the Bengali wishes in this post ourselves, so copy them freely. A call still means more than a forward, though.

slides.title: Kojagari Lakshmi Puja: who is awake tonight?
slides.sub: The full-moon puja a few days after Dashami

slides.title: Ko jagarti?
slides.body: Kojagari comes from the Sanskrit ko jagarti, who is awake? On this full-moon night, tradition says, Lakshmi goes from house to house asking it, and blesses the homes she finds awake.

slides.title: The full moon after Dashami
slides.body: It falls on Sharad Purnima, the full moon of Ashwin, a few days after Bijoya Dashami (21 October in 2026). The date and hours of the Purnima tithi change every year: check your local panjika.

slides.title: The king who bought Alakshmi
slides.body: A king buys an unsold image of Alakshmi, and good fortune leaves his palace. The queen keeps the Kojagari vow: she cleans, lights lamps and stays awake all night. Lakshmi returns.

slides.title: Lamp lit, home clean, stay awake
slides.ask: Send it to whoever draws the alpana

caption.en:
Kojagari Lakshmi Puja after Durga Puja: the Kolkata home puja on Sharad Purnima 🌕

Kojagari comes from ko jagarti, who is awake? Lakshmi is said to visit homes on this full-moon night and stay where she finds the lamp lit and the household awake.

It falls a few days after Bijoya Dashami, which is Wednesday 21 October this year. The date and hours of the Purnima tithi change every year, so check your local panjika.

Alpana in rice paste, little footprints walking in from the door, khichuri, narkel naru, khoi and the Lakshmir panchali read aloud. Every family does it a little differently.

Who draws the alpana in your home? Tell us in the comments 👇

slides.title: Eco-friendly pujo, at home and in the para
slides.sub: Going greener often means going back to the old ways

slides.title: Clay, not plaster of Paris
slides.body: Straw, bamboo and unbaked clay break down in water. Plaster of Paris sets hard and dissolves very slowly. Look for an idol with no thermocol, or ornaments you can remove before immersion.

slides.title: Gentler paint
slides.body: Ask the artisan whether they use water-based, non-toxic or natural colours. Choose lightly painted or unpainted idols for home pujas, and skip glitter and metallic sprays.

slides.title: Before the immersion
slides.body: Take off flowers, garlands, cloth, ornaments and plastic first. Use an artificial pond or immersion tank if there's one near you. Rules vary and change, so check current local notices.

slides.title: In the pandal
items: Bhog on sal-leaf, banana-leaf or steel
Clear bins for wet and dry waste
LED lights, off in the small hours
Cloth signs instead of plastic flex
Reuse bamboo, jute, frames and panels
Moderate sound, switched off at night

slides.title: At home
items: A small unpainted clay idol, or a ghot
Fresh flowers, mango leaves, rice alpana
Steel or leaf plates for prasad
Immerse in a tub, pour the clay into a plant

slides.title: Greener is also older
slides.ask: Send it to your para committee

caption.en:
Eco-friendly Durga Puja in Kolkata: clay idols, cleaner immersion and less plastic in the para 🌿

Clay, straw, natural colours, flowers and leaf plates are the oldest parts of pujo. So going greener often means going back. Plaster of Paris sets hard and dissolves very slowly in water, while unbaked clay returns to the earth far more readily.

At home, you can immerse a small clay idol in a bucket or tub and pour the clay into a plant, if your family priest agrees. Immersion rules change, so check current notices from the pollution control board, the municipality and the police.
